subcomponents.title: Uses scene-kit APIs without bypassing or duplicating them

criteria.rationale: Talk passes its steps to the shared Presentation host. SampleScene composes scene-kit nodes and Presence, while Presentation delegates scene mounting to Stage. The demo uses the reusable boundaries for orchestration and entity motion.
evidence: Talk renders <Presentation steps={steps}>.
SampleScene uses Box, Arrow, SymbolChip, Emphasis, Label, Frame, SceneLayer, and Presence from the presentation kit.
Stage mounts the active step's Scene.

subcomponents.title: Uses stable identities and appropriate grouped-scene architecture

criteria.rationale: All nine step entries use SampleScene and the same groupKey. Stage uses that key for the scene mount, so payload changes update the grouped scene. Separately, SampleScene passes presentation-owned entity IDs to kit nodes; those nodes use each ID as a Motion layoutId.
evidence: Every entry in steps has groupKey 'one-evolving-scene', Scene: SampleScene, and a distinct beat payload.
Stage keys the mounted scene and LayoutGroup from groupKey.
SampleScene supplies IDs from entities to its persistent kit nodes; each cited node maps id to layoutId.

subcomponents.title: Maintains clear boundaries and scope discipline

criteria.rationale: The delivered Talk supplies the required title, Presentation forwards it, and Header renders it in browse mode. Step data stays in the presentation's step list and payload-driven Scene; shared chrome and stage behavior stay in the kit.
evidence: Talk passes the presentation title as a prop.
Presentation passes title to Header for both its populated and empty states.
Header renders title in its h1 when browsing.

criteria.rationale: Progress and table-of-contents controls expose aria-current with a stable active-state hook. Presentation-local CSS styles those active hooks and the attribution. The default attribution link is implemented in the project-local Footer.
evidence: Footer and Toc set aria-current and data-presentation-active from the current index.
The demo stylesheet targets active progress and table-of-contents controls and styles .presentation-attribution.
Footer renders the default 'made by and-scene' GitHub link with an attribution hook.

criteria.rationale: The registry loads the demo's Talk, which supplies local steps to the generic Presentation host. The demo's entity IDs, scene logic, and styling reside in its presentation folder; the shared host consumes the step contract without demo-specific branches.
evidence: The registry entry loads the demo Talk.
Talk passes its local steps to Presentation.
The complete presentation-local implementation consists of Talk, steps, entities, Scene, and its stylesheet; Presentation delegates step rendering to Stage.

subcomponents.title: Step model, stable identity, and typed boundary

criteria.rationale: Each rendered step supplies an ID, era, title, caption, scene component, and payload. The active step drives both narration and the scene.
evidence: StepMeta and Step define the step fields; Presentation selects steps[nav.index] and passes it to Stage and Footer.

criteria.rationale: Displayed step numbers come from array positions, so reordering steps changes their numbers without editing step data.
evidence: Footer renders index + 1 in the marker and i + 1 in progress buttons.

criteria.rationale: The generic Step type ties a scene's payload prop to its payload value, and Stage passes the selected value through that boundary.
evidence: Step<TPayload> requires Scene: ComponentType<SceneProps<TPayload>> and payload: TPayload; Stage renders <Scene payload={step.payload} />.

subcomponents.title: Entity transitions and persistent grouped scenes

criteria.rationale: Entities with stable IDs use Motion layout animation within a persistent grouped scene.
evidence: Box renders motion.div with layout and layoutId={id}; Stage supplies LayoutGroup, while the sample repeats entity IDs across beats.

criteria.rationale: The continuing layout path and newcomer opacity path consume the same settlement duration: entry delay equals the layout duration.
evidence: entityMotion uses LAYOUT_T for layout duration and ENTER_DELAY for opacity delay; constants set ENTER_DELAY = LAYOUT_T. Box and Arrow both spread entityMotion onto their motion elements.

criteria.rationale: Ordinary sample entities are conditionally rendered inside Presence, which retains them during exit; a focused browser test checks that departing cards remain before removal.
evidence: SampleScene wraps its conditional card list in Presence. The browser test moves backward from four cards, asserts four still exist immediately, then waits for the count to become one.

criteria.rationale: Steps sharing a group key retain the same scene wrapper and component while receiving a new payload.
evidence: Stage keys its motion scene by groupKey; all sample steps use the same groupKey and SampleScene. The focused test changes payload from 1 to 2 and asserts the scene mounted once.

criteria.rationale: The grouped scene and its continuing keyed child remain mounted across payload updates, so their initial entry state is not replayed.
evidence: Stage retains the same keyed scene for a group; SampleScene keeps the sample-you Box in the same component at every beat. The grouped-scene test asserts one mount after advancing.

criteria.rationale: The grouped sample implements one evolving diagram: continuing conversation entities remain while cards, controls, verification, and the final frame are added by beat.
evidence: SampleScene derives conditional entities and card counts from payload.beat; every sample step points to that scene with the same group key and a successive beat.

subcomponents.title: Present/browse modes, navigation, controls, and boundaries

criteria.rationale: Present mode retains the active step title and marker while removing browse caption, contents, progress, and previous/next controls.
evidence: Footer always renders marker and h2, but gates caption, progress, and controls on browse; Presentation gates Toc on browse.

criteria.rationale: Browse mode renders the active title and wrapping caption, wide-viewport contents, previous/next controls, and progress indicators.
evidence: Footer renders these active-step elements in browse mode; Toc renders at widths of at least 960px; presentation CSS permits caption wrapping within a max width.

criteria.rationale: Changing modes updates only mode state; the current index remains in place.
evidence: usePresentationNav's toggleMode calls setMode without changing index. The focused test switches modes at index 1 and asserts data-step-index remains 1.

criteria.rationale: The window key handler advances on ArrowRight, Space, or PageDown and reverses on ArrowLeft or PageUp.
evidence: usePresentationNav maps those keys to next and prev; the focused test dispatches ArrowRight and asserts the second caption appears.

criteria.rationale: Swipe handling measures horizontal distance alone. It records neither vertical movement nor touch count, so predominantly vertical and multi-touch gestures can navigate.
evidence: Presentation stores only touchX and advances when absolute dx exceeds 48; no focused vertical or multi-touch rejection assertions are present in the inspected navigation tests.

criteria.rationale: Progress buttons jump to their indexed step, and contents buttons jump to the first step of an era.
evidence: Footer progress buttons call onGoTo(i); Toc calls onGoTo(first). The focused test clicks Finish and asserts the third caption.

criteria.rationale: Current progress and contents controls expose semantic current state and stable active-state attributes.
evidence: Footer and Toc set aria-current='step' and data-presentation-active for the active item; the focused test asserts the current progress control after a jump.

criteria.rationale: Presentation key handling returns when focus is on an interactive control, preserving that control's keyboard behavior.
evidence: usePresentationNav excludes BUTTON, A, INPUT, TEXTAREA, and SELECT targets; the focused test sends ArrowRight to the Next button and asserts the step does not change.

criteria.rationale: Previous navigation clamps the index at zero.
evidence: prev uses Math.max(0, i - 1); the focused test clicks Previous on the first step and asserts the first caption remains.

criteria.rationale: Next navigation clamps the index at the last step.
evidence: next uses Math.min(lastIndex, i + 1); the focused test reaches the third step, clicks Next, and asserts the third caption remains.

demo-integration.rationale: Talk passes its steps to the shared Presentation host. SampleScene composes scene-kit nodes and Presence, while Presentation delegates scene mounting to Stage. The demo uses the reusable boundaries for orchestration and entity motion.
evidence: Talk renders <Presentation steps={steps}>.
SampleScene uses Box, Arrow, SymbolChip, Emphasis, Label, Frame, SceneLayer, and Presence from the presentation kit.
Stage mounts the active step's Scene.

demo-integration.rationale: All nine step entries use SampleScene and the same groupKey. Stage uses that key for the scene mount, so payload changes update the grouped scene. Separately, SampleScene passes presentation-owned entity IDs to kit nodes; those nodes use each ID as a Motion layoutId.
evidence: Every entry in steps has groupKey 'one-evolving-scene', Scene: SampleScene, and a distinct beat payload.
Stage keys the mounted scene and LayoutGroup from groupKey.
SampleScene supplies IDs from entities to its persistent kit nodes; each cited node maps id to layoutId.

demo-integration.rationale: The delivered Talk supplies the required title, Presentation forwards it, and Header renders it in browse mode. Step data stays in the presentation's step list and payload-driven Scene; shared chrome and stage behavior stay in the kit.
evidence: Talk passes the presentation title as a prop.
Presentation passes title to Header for both its populated and empty states.
Header renders title in its h1 when browsing.

demo-integration.rationale: Progress and table-of-contents controls expose aria-current with a stable active-state hook. Presentation-local CSS styles those active hooks and the attribution. The default attribution link is implemented in the project-local Footer.
evidence: Footer and Toc set aria-current and data-presentation-active from the current index.
The demo stylesheet targets active progress and table-of-contents controls and styles .presentation-attribution.
Footer renders the default 'made by and-scene' GitHub link with an attribution hook.

demo-integration.rationale: The registry loads the demo's Talk, which supplies local steps to the generic Presentation host. The demo's entity IDs, scene logic, and styling reside in its presentation folder; the shared host consumes the step contract without demo-specific branches.
evidence: The registry entry loads the demo Talk.
Talk passes its local steps to Presentation.
The complete presentation-local implementation consists of Talk, steps, entities, Scene, and its stylesheet; Presentation delegates step rendering to Stage.

scene-kit.rationale: Each rendered step supplies an ID, era, title, caption, scene component, and payload. The active step drives both narration and the scene.
evidence: StepMeta and Step define the step fields; Presentation selects steps[nav.index] and passes it to Stage and Footer.

scene-kit.rationale: Displayed step numbers come from array positions, so reordering steps changes their numbers without editing step data.
evidence: Footer renders index + 1 in the marker and i + 1 in progress buttons.

scene-kit.rationale: The generic Step type ties a scene's payload prop to its payload value, and Stage passes the selected value through that boundary.
evidence: Step<TPayload> requires Scene: ComponentType<SceneProps<TPayload>> and payload: TPayload; Stage renders <Scene payload={step.payload} />.

scene-kit.rationale: Entities with stable IDs use Motion layout animation within a persistent grouped scene.
evidence: Box renders motion.div with layout and layoutId={id}; Stage supplies LayoutGroup, while the sample repeats entity IDs across beats.

scene-kit.rationale: The continuing layout path and newcomer opacity path consume the same settlement duration: entry delay equals the layout duration.
evidence: entityMotion uses LAYOUT_T for layout duration and ENTER_DELAY for opacity delay; constants set ENTER_DELAY = LAYOUT_T. Box and Arrow both spread entityMotion onto their motion elements.

scene-kit.rationale: Ordinary sample entities are conditionally rendered inside Presence, which retains them during exit; a focused browser test checks that departing cards remain before removal.
evidence: SampleScene wraps its conditional card list in Presence. The browser test moves backward from four cards, asserts four still exist immediately, then waits for the count to become one.

scene-kit.rationale: Steps sharing a group key retain the same scene wrapper and component while receiving a new payload.
evidence: Stage keys its motion scene by groupKey; all sample steps use the same groupKey and SampleScene. The focused test changes payload from 1 to 2 and asserts the scene mounted once.

scene-kit.rationale: The grouped scene and its continuing keyed child remain mounted across payload updates, so their initial entry state is not replayed.
evidence: Stage retains the same keyed scene for a group; SampleScene keeps the sample-you Box in the same component at every beat. The grouped-scene test asserts one mount after advancing.

scene-kit.rationale: The grouped sample implements one evolving diagram: continuing conversation entities remain while cards, controls, verification, and the final frame are added by beat.
evidence: SampleScene derives conditional entities and card counts from payload.beat; every sample step points to that scene with the same group key and a successive beat.

scene-kit.rationale: Present mode retains the active step title and marker while removing browse caption, contents, progress, and previous/next controls.
evidence: Footer always renders marker and h2, but gates caption, progress, and controls on browse; Presentation gates Toc on browse.

scene-kit.rationale: Browse mode renders the active title and wrapping caption, wide-viewport contents, previous/next controls, and progress indicators.
evidence: Footer renders these active-step elements in browse mode; Toc renders at widths of at least 960px; presentation CSS permits caption wrapping within a max width.

scene-kit.rationale: Changing modes updates only mode state; the current index remains in place.
evidence: usePresentationNav's toggleMode calls setMode without changing index. The focused test switches modes at index 1 and asserts data-step-index remains 1.

scene-kit.rationale: The window key handler advances on ArrowRight, Space, or PageDown and reverses on ArrowLeft or PageUp.
evidence: usePresentationNav maps those keys to next and prev; the focused test dispatches ArrowRight and asserts the second caption appears.

scene-kit.rationale: Swipe handling measures horizontal distance alone. It records neither vertical movement nor touch count, so predominantly vertical and multi-touch gestures can navigate.
evidence: Presentation stores only touchX and advances when absolute dx exceeds 48; no focused vertical or multi-touch rejection assertions are present in the inspected navigation tests.

scene-kit.rationale: Progress buttons jump to their indexed step, and contents buttons jump to the first step of an era.
evidence: Footer progress buttons call onGoTo(i); Toc calls onGoTo(first). The focused test clicks Finish and asserts the third caption.

scene-kit.rationale: Current progress and contents controls expose semantic current state and stable active-state attributes.
evidence: Footer and Toc set aria-current='step' and data-presentation-active for the active item; the focused test asserts the current progress control after a jump.

scene-kit.rationale: Presentation key handling returns when focus is on an interactive control, preserving that control's keyboard behavior.
evidence: usePresentationNav excludes BUTTON, A, INPUT, TEXTAREA, and SELECT targets; the focused test sends ArrowRight to the Next button and asserts the step does not change.

scene-kit.rationale: Previous navigation clamps the index at zero.
evidence: prev uses Math.max(0, i - 1); the focused test clicks Previous on the first step and asserts the first caption remains.

scene-kit.rationale: Next navigation clamps the index at the last step.
evidence: next uses Math.min(lastIndex, i + 1); the focused test reaches the third step, clicks Next, and asserts the third caption remains.

scene-kit.rationale: The canvas uses one scale factor, but its window-centered stage can overlap browse chrome at an ordinary 1280×600 viewport. The computed factor is about 0.905, leaving a 344px canvas centered from y=128 to y=472, while the 150px footer begins at y=450.
evidence: useFitScale subtracts top and bottom reserves from viewport height; sample CSS centers the fixed-height stage at 50% of the window and places a minimum-height footer at the bottom, without shifting t…

scene-kit.rationale: The rendered stage defaults to the approved 880×380 authored canvas.
evidence: DESIGN_W and DESIGN_H are 880 and 380; Stage uses them as default width and height and applies both to the canvas element.

scene-kit.rationale: The kit exposes stable selectors for its root, stage, canvas, scene, chrome, controls, and entities.
evidence: Presentation and Stage emit data-presentation attributes; Footer exposes control and active-state hooks; Box exposes a node hook and data-entity-id.

scene-kit.rationale: Kit primitives set structural positioning and motion without imposing colors, backgrounds, borders, or typography; presentation CSS supplies those treatments.
evidence: Box's rendered element receives caller className and style with no visual defaults. The focused test asserts empty inline color, background, border, and shadow; sample CSS defines the entity trea…

scene-kit.rationale: The scaffold uses the kit without a required styling framework.
evidence: The bootstrap manifest lists React, Motion, and build tools without a CSS framework; the bootstrap test copies the scaffold, checks kit parity, and builds and renders it.

scene-kit.rationale: Authored scene elements can use explicit coordinates within the fixed canvas.
evidence: SampleScene passes pixel left and top positions to kit nodes; presentation CSS absolutely positions the diagram entities and connectors inside the scene.

scene-kit.rationale: The kit itself renders the default and-scene GitHub link and positions it at the footer's bottom-right corner.
evidence: Footer renders the link with href, label, and inline position:absolute; right:0; bottom:0. Its parent footer is positioned by kit markup.

scene-kit.rationale: The default link has stable class and data attributes that host or presentation CSS can target.
evidence: Footer assigns presentation-attribution and data-presentation-attribution; sample CSS targets the class.

scene-kit.rationale: The top-left brand container is empty by default and accepts explicit host branding.
evidence: Header renders only the optional brand prop in its brand container; Presentation forwards its optional brand prop. The focused test asserts the default container is empty.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill requires asking for missing topic, visual direction, and step details one question at a time, waiting for each answer.
evidence: Section 1 explicitly requires sequential questions and answers for missing creation details.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill permits the user to proceed with partial details and directs the agent to build without a completeness gate.
evidence: Section 1 says to record open details, make reasonable connective choices, and proceed when the user chooses partial detail.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill explicitly bypasses further questions when the prompt is complete.
evidence: Section 1 states that a complete prompt needs no further questions.

presentation-skill.rationale: A focused bootstrap test copies the template into a previously absent standalone app path, checks scaffold files and dependencies, installs packages there, and builds and renders the app.
evidence: The 'materializes outside the source tree' test creates a temporary target, copies bootstrap into it, asserts kit, registry, build config, and dependency presence, then runs npm ci, build, an…

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill instructs use of an app with all anchors, but no focused test constructs that state and verifies that existing scaffold files are retained.
evidence: The bootstrap test starts with an absent target; it does not exercise the all-anchors-present branch.

presentation-skill.rationale: There is no focused executable evidence that a target with only some scaffold anchors receives just the missing contracts while preserving existing ones.
evidence: The bootstrap test copies the complete template into a new target; it does not construct a partial scaffold.

presentation-skill.rationale: The scaffold test checks that the host reset has no palette, font, or theme variables and no Tailwind dependency; a kit test checks that its Box primitive injects no color, background, border, or shadow.
evidence: The bootstrap style assertions and 'uses custom unstyled primitives' test exercise style neutrality; the template host CSS contains only reset and sizing rules.

presentation-skill.rationale: The executable test derives the template path from the test file’s repository root, not from SKILL.md. It confirms installation in the copied app but does not exercise the required skill-relative template resolution.
evidence: The bootstrap constant is built from the test module location; npm ci runs with cwd set to the copied app.

presentation-skill.rationale: No focused test constructs a monorepo and verifies that the app and its dependencies land under presentations/ without changing root configuration.
evidence: The only scaffold materialization test copies directly into a temporary app path.

presentation-skill.rationale: The empty-target test does not construct a pre-existing standalone project or verify the standalone-project target selection branch.
evidence: The tested app path does not exist before the full template copy.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill says to confirm a destination in a nonempty project missing anchors, but no focused test or verified workflow evidence constructs that ambiguous state and checks the choice before writing.
evidence: The bootstrap test uses a new target and contains no confirmation or destination-choice branch.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill requires registering a new slug and route; the registry supplies slug-to-loader entries and main.tsx selects and renders the loader matching the URL.
evidence: Section 4 directs registration; presentations is a slug/title/load registry, and main.tsx matches the normalized route and renders the selected lazy component.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill assigns visual design to each presentation’s CSS. The presentation template imports its own stylesheet, and the delivered presentation does the same.
evidence: The template Talk imports ./style.css; the delivered Talk imports its local stylesheet, which defines the presentation’s visual rules.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill explicitly requires adding new registry entries without editing or deleting others and preserving unrelated presentations.
